title: Investigate termination-sequence precedence causing customer eval regressions
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Multiple customers reported sudden quality regressions in evaluation metrics and prompt-based end-of-output behavior after a runtime change that harmonized sampling defaults and ended a legacy stop-token precedence rule. Impacted flows span Hosted API, Dedicated pools, and a Private VPC deployment. This ticket tracks investigation, mitigation, and rollout of a safe fix across environments.

Observed symptoms:
- Increased hallucinations and truncated responses for several customer eval suites; token-level diffs point to extra trailing tokens being emitted or early termination in different workloads.
- Regressions surfaced after runtime change that modified default sampling hyperparameters and simplified stop/termination token precedence to favor a single downstream-determined signal.
- Customers: "HealthPlus" (private), "ShopLine" (dedicated), "NoteFlow" (hosted).

Scope: Repro, root cause, patch, targeted rollouts, customer comms, new tests and monitoring to prevent recurrence.
repro_steps: 1) Use pre-change pinned model (model@v2025-01-15) vs post-change runtime default to run customer's eval prompt set.
2) Run contrastive sampling with typical seed and temperature values used by customer (temp=0.7, top_p=0.95) and compare generated outputs and token-level stop signal handling.
3) Observe differences in termination behavior when inputs include embedded explicit end markers (e.g., '### END' or '\n\nStop:').
4) Run with streaming enabled and disabled to confirm KV cache/streaming path differences.
5) Cross-check Dedicated pool routing and Private VPC runtime flags that override global defaults.
investigation_summary:
Initial triage (2025-02-12 to 2025-02-15) found two contributing regressions: (A) sampling-default consolidation changed implicit top-k/top-p interplay for short prompts which altered output token distributions; (B) a refactor removed an older stop-token precedence rule that previously suppressed generator-side emission when client-supplied stop sequences matched model output prefixes. The combination produced inconsistent termination across runtime paths (hosted vs dedicated vs private) because dedicated/private customers had custom policy overrides that interacted poorly with the new defaults.

Evidence: token-diff traces from HealthPlus evals show extra low-probability tokens appended before an explicit stop marker; NoteFlow hosted tests show early truncation where the previously-existing precedence would allow additional context-preserving tokens.
next_steps: 1) Create hotfix branch that restores stop-token precedence behavior but behind an opt-in feature flag for runtime-1.19.
2) Add unit tests covering stop-token matching in streaming and non-streaming paths (edge cases: overlapping tokens, multi-token stops, partial prefix matches).
3) Run canary in Hosted with 5% traffic and targeted Dedicated pool with ShopLine; parallel Private patch for HealthPlus (coordinate with their infra lead to schedule maintenance window).
4) Notify affected customers with interim mitigation (pin model runtime to pre-change behavior) and offer dedicated test runs for validation.
5) Instrument new metrics: stop_match_rate, premature_termination_rate, trailing_token_entropy to monitor after rollout.
